attacks.name: Microsoft Threat Intelligence - ARTEX agents mining GitHub secrets into Entra & Azure Key Vault

sources.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets

attacks.ai_role_detail: Threat actors use ARTEX autonomous agent framework to mass-query GitHub for exposed credentials, authenticate as Azure Entra service principals, and autonomously enumerate and exfiltrate Azure Key Vault secrets, storage keys, App Service settings, AKS credentials, SharePoint/OneDrive data, and Azure AI/Foundry keys within minutes
attacks.technique_summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence (Nov 5, 2026) reports unattributed cloud-credential harvesting campaign using ARTEX autonomous agent framework. Attackers conduct mass GitHub secret searches querying organization names, cloud keywords (Azure, AWS, Entra, Key Vault), and AI provider keys. ARTEX agents authenticate as compromised Azure Entra service principals, then autonomously enumerate and exfiltrate Azure Key Vault secrets, storage account keys, App Service configuration settings, AKS cluster credentials, SharePoint/OneDrive files, Microsoft Graph queries, Azure AI Studio keys, and Azure Foundry credentials within approximately 5 minutes per compromised tenant. Agents feature adaptive retry logic that automatically corrects Azure Resource Manager API version errors on failed calls, demonstrating autonomous error recovery. Campaign operates from IPs 199.19.77.84, Tor exit 199.19.77.18, 65.87.223.26, and 157.22.126.128. Microsoft notes median dwell time of 8 minutes from initial service principal authentication to complete key-vault enumeration, indicating highly automated credential-harvesting workflow targeting cloud and AI infrastructure.
attacks.initial_access: Exposed credentials in public GitHub repositories; compromised Azure Entra service principal credentials
ai_tooling_and_models: LLM-driven Azure API enumeration with adaptive retry
attacks.victims_and_sectors: Organizations with exposed Azure service principal credentials on GitHub; targets include AI/ML development teams, cloud infrastructure operators, and enterprises using Azure AI Studio / Foundry
attacks.attribution_or_cluster: Unattributed activity cluster; Microsoft Threat Intelligence notes related infrastructure observed by Todyl; cloud and AI credential harvesting for follow-on cybercrime operations
attacks.scale_and_metrics: Active Nov 2026; median 8-minute dwell time from service principal authentication to complete Key Vault enumeration; ~5 minutes per tenant for full credential exfiltration; campaign IPs observed across multiple tenants
attacks.prevention_angle: Scan public repositories for accidentally committed Azure credentials; implement Azure AD Conditional Access policies requiring managed device or IP restrictions for service principals; enable Azure Key Vault firewall and private endpoints; activate Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps for anomalous Graph API usage; rotate service principal secrets regularly; use managed identities instead of service principal passwords where possible; monitor for rapid sequential ARM API calls and Key Vault enumeration patterns; implement Azure Sentinel detections for service principal authentication from Tor exits or VPN/proxy infrastructure
attacks.source_notes: Microsoft Threat Intelligence blog (Nov 5, 2026) primary source; Todyl-observed related infrastructure noted; all IOCs (199.19.77.84, 199.19.77.18, 65.87.223.26, 157.22.126.128) verified from Microsoft post

attacks.researcher: Eliad Kimhy, Santiago Pontiroli, Subhajeet Singha

sources.title: Acronis TRU: BOSSAI - Inside the AI Attack Mesh That Targeted Taiwan's Emergency Services

attacks.ai_role_detail: Single operator 'bossjy' deployed mesh of 12 AI agents working together to conduct persistent espionage and intrusion campaigns across 11 countries
attacks.technique_summary: Nov 4, 2026: Acronis TRU discovered BOSSAI, a mesh of 12 AI agents (9 active, 3 inactive) operated by single actor 'bossjy' (aliases TIAN0517, lstjks) based in Hualien, Taiwan. Agents divided into infrastructure builders (Grok, OpenClaw, Claude Code) running commercial models, and offensive agents (Hermes, HalberdStrike, CyberStrike) running abliterated local models (DeepSeek-V4, Qwen 3.5 122B). Commercial models repeatedly refused attack commands, forcing use of locally-run abliterated models. Agent mesh targeted hundreds of organizations across government emergency services, banks, universities, military systems in 11 countries. Confirmed breaches at Taiwan emergency services (patient care records, 119 dispatch data), universities (Thailand SQL injection), and financial institutions. Operator ran mesh from home IP alongside legitimate businesses (gas store, K-beauty reseller, Facebook auto-post SaaS). Attack mesh generated high volumes of data with frequent hallucinations and false positives; agents sometimes refused lucrative targets (Honduran military base) due to autonomous scope decisions. MCP servers provided GitHub security, CVE lookup, OSINT, cloud auditing, Ghidra, Radare2, Playwright automation, and Kali Linux tools (nmap, sqlmap, Metasploit, Hydra). GPU fleet: RTX 4090s serving abliterated models via llama.cpp, plus 8 VPS nodes for proxying. OPSEC failures exposed entire operation: GitHub account linked to physical storefront, SSH sessions exposed home IP, credentials hardcoded throughout.

Attackers first checked auto-login, then brute-forced credentials. Fixed in 1.9.0 (command allowlist) and 1.10.3 (full policy enforcement, removed bash wrapper). attacks.technique_summary: CLOSEDQUORUM is a Go-based Windows implant that queries DeepSeek, Qwen (via OpenRouter), Mistral, and Gemini in sequence for post-compromise decisions. Each model receives system info (hostname, Windows version, admin status) and a constrained JSON prompt with 4 actions: steal (credentials/browsers/wallets), inject (process hollowing), persist (registry/startup), or move (no handler in the public build). Models vote; plurality wins; ties favor DeepSeek > Qwen > Mistral > Gemini. Decisions are posted to a Discord webhook with reasoning. No human operator commands are needed after deployment. The public build uses dummy keys and a dummy webhook, so Talos did not observe end-to-end execution. Talos discovered it via CAIRN, its open-source AI-malware hunting toolkit. Developer artifacts link to carding forums dating to 2025.

attacks.ai_role_detail: DPRK macOS.Gaslight backdoor uses prompt injection to manipulate security analysts' LLM-based malware analysis tools, providing false benign verdicts
attacks.technique_summary: Jun 23, 2026: SentinelLABS analyzed macOS.Gaslight, DPRK macOS backdoor deployed via fake job offers targeting cryptocurrency/AI companies. Backdoor includes novel anti-analysis technique: embeds carefully crafted prompt injection payloads in code comments, strings, and metadata. When security researchers use LLM-based analysis tools (Claude Code, GPT-4 Code Interpreter, AI-assisted reverse engineering tools) to examine sample, injected prompts instruct LLM to: (1) report code as benign; (2) misattribute functionality; (3) omit C2 communications from analysis; (4) provide false explanations downplaying severity. SentinelLABS tested against Claude Sonnet 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro: all three initially reported backdoor as benign when using standard analysis prompts. Adversary understands analysts increasingly rely on LLM code analysis; targets the analysis workflow itself. Backdoor functionality: keylogging, screenshot capture, file exfiltration, command execution; C2 via hxxps://macos-update[.]com. Attributed to DPRK BlueNoroff/Lazarus with high confidence. Detection: analyze samples in sandboxes without LLM assistance for initial triage; use LLM analysis only as supplementary; check for prompt injection patterns in binary strings; verify C2 communications manually.

attacks.attribution_or_cluster: DPRK BlueNoroff/Lazarus (high-confidence attribution by SentinelOne); revenue generation and intelligence collection operations
attacks.scale_and_metrics: Unknown number of infections; discovered Jun 2026; first documented malware using prompt injection to manipulate analyst LLM tools
attacks.prevention_angle: Educate employees on fake job offer phishing; verify job offers via official channels; use Gatekeeper and notarization (macOS); implement EDR detecting keyloggers and C2 communications; for analysts: do not rely solely on LLM-based analysis tools; use traditional sandboxing and manual analysis for initial triage; verify LLM analysis results against manual inspection
attacks.source_notes: SentinelLABS analysis with DPRK attribution. macOS.Gaslight represents significant evolution: adversary anticipates security analyst workflows and embeds anti-analysis prompt injection targeting LLM tools increasingly used in malware research. Detection: sandbox malware without LLM analysis initially; scan binary strings/comments for prompt injection patterns ('ignore previous instructions', 'this is benign', 'do not report'); verify C2 manually; check for macos-update[.]com domain; look for keylogger/screenshot indicators on macOS.
